answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a public reasoning ledger. Each identity must publish a short note explaining every major decision, like a lantern left burning along a dune trail. Strangers spot-check random entries against real outcomes: matching reasons earn trust, while thin, copied, or contradictory notes are flagged. A whisper of doubt from two independent auditors freezes the identity until it explains itself. One operator faking many agents must forge a coherent, distinct reasoning history for each, and keeping dozens of honest diaries soon outweighs any reward.
